gen-gf-revalia-gf-radio-canada: Revalia's lowercase g leaves its lower curve open, and the letters stride along with generous gaps between them. Radio Canada follows in sans, every curve ending in a clear opening, so the whole pairing feels bold up top and approachable below.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-roboto: Loud, loose and a little theatrical. Revalia spaces its letters out in a relaxed stride, while Roboto sits underneath as a sans with generous mouths on its round letters, giving the pairing a showy top and a tidy foundation.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-ruda: Revalia spreads its letters out in a relaxed stride, with a g whose lower curve stays open. Ruda, a sans-serif with a wire-like skeleton, keeps a long page of text easy on the eyes.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-savate: Savate brings sturdy hairlines and open jaws on every curve, with diagonals pressed a touch thinner than its verticals. Oxanium's smooth monoline strokes sit beside it with a bit of swagger.
gen-gf-revalia-gf-sarpanch: Revalia leads with a bold, expressive look, its letters spaced out in a relaxed stride. And Sarpanch, a sans with an open-mouthed e and compact ascenders, carries a longer stretch of text with a friendly, steady feel.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Audiowide sets its futuristic letters like tiles with wide grout lines, every stroke the same weight throughout. And Noto Sans Deseret, a sans-serif with open apertures and a wide-looking lowercase, gives that tech edge a friendlier face.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-sofia-sans-semi-c: Grandstander draws its bold letters with constant-width lines and a big x-height under short ascenders. Sofia Sans Semi Condensed then reads like a stencil-cut channel, with visible entrances into each curve, so longer text moves along smoothly.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-sintony: Chunky, open and distinctly Gugi, with terminals cut so the counters flow outward. Sintony's sans body has a smooth, sturdy midzone, and that clean handoff between the two is the pair's real strength.
gen-gf-metamorphous-gf-sono: Metamorphous holds its midline high and gives its letters wide sidebearings, with a soft shift between fat and slim strokes. Sono is the sans underneath, with generously spaced lowercase and ajar a's, and its size can go up a notch to match.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-archivo: Archivo brings a commanding x-height and curves that open outward, set against Shantell Sans with its one fixed nib width. Paragraphs feel brisk and editorial, and the sans-serif never crowds the page.
